title: The cosmic bat: NGC 1788
caption: The nebula NGC 1788 in Orion, imaged by the MPG/ESO 2.2-metre telescope at La Silla
celestial: NGC 1788 · constellation Orion · about 3000 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: A delicate, ghostly cloud glows in this finely detailed ESO image. This is the nebula NGC 1788, which lies about 3000 light-years away in a dark and often overlooked corner of the constellation Orion, somewhat isolated from Orion's bright stars.

Isolation does not mean independence. The powerful winds and light of those bright stars strongly affect the nebula, sculpting its shape and helping to make it home to a multitude of infant stars. NGC 1788 is catalogued as a reflection nebula, a cloud of dust that shines mainly by scattering the light of nearby stars.
Nebulae like this show how star birth in one place can be shaped by stars elsewhere. Radiation and winds travel across space, pressing on gas and dust and influencing where and how new stars form.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (26.44 x 19.89 arcminutes) and distance (3000 light years), the frame spans roughly 23 × 17 light-years. Its light set out about 3,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This visible-light image from the Wide Field Imager combines blue, green and red filters with one that isolates glowing hydrogen. The colour assigned to each filter isn't published.
understand.eye: Long camera exposures gather far more light than the eye can, revealing a faint nebula that would be hard to see directly.

explore: Taken with La Silla's MPG/ESO 2.2-metre telescope and its Wide Field Imager, the picture combines blue, green and red filters with a special filter tuned to the glow of hydrogen gas. The frame spans about 30 arcminutes, with north up and east to the left.
alt: A faint, delicate nebula in a dark region of sky.
